chapters.title: Translate through CSV or TSV
chapters.intro: The translation spreadsheet preserves the source text and stable record identity. Edit the translation column while keeping the exported structure intact.
steps: Inspect editable text in Text & layout. Open Translation spreadsheet and download CSV or TSV for the selected source and definition.
Keep every stable ID, original-text field and control column. Edit only translation. Preserve delimiters, quoted multiline fields and the same file format when saving.
Import the sheet back into the same source context. Review unmapped characters, protected controls and encoded byte capacity for each changed record.
Preview the translation plan, create a separate build and test menus, dialogue, line breaks and transitions using the actual font and game logic.
chapters.result: Changed rows map back to the exported records. Original controls are protected and every translation fits its declared encoding and allocation.
chapters.note: Character count and encoded byte count can differ. A spreadsheet that silently reformats IDs or line breaks can invalidate the import. Shorten text or correct an established allocation rather than bypassing limits.

details.title: A useful first round-trip
details.text: Export a sheet, change one short line and reimport it before translating hundreds of rows. Keep the original export as a reference and a project backup outside the workspace.

details.title: Text preview limits
details.text: A system-font comparison helps review wording. It does not establish glyph availability, game-window width or dialogue behavior. Use declared font/layout measurements and native playtesting for those checks.

chapters.caption: The longer proposed string exceeds the nine available text bytes. This is a capacity demonstration, not a new built translation. Shorten the proposal or use an independently verified relocation workflow; never write through the next record.

chapters.title: Declare text, fonts and layout limits
chapters.intro: Text bytes need an encoding and storage layout. Font and window measurements add useful checks when those formats are explicitly declared.
steps: Declare the text offset, slot capacity, encoding and terminator, or load a verified definition for the exact source. Add pointer information only when its location and mapping are established.
Inspect records and visible control tokens. Edit wording while preserving required controls and segment boundaries. Read capacity and unmapped-character feedback.
For declared fonts and menu/dialogue layouts, inspect the actual decoded-font canvas, glyph metrics and available dimensions. Treat a measured overflow as a concrete issue in that declared layout.
Review the exact plan, including pointer or integrity changes, build and test the actual screen. Inspect the following record or menu item for unintended damage.
chapters.result: The edited record fits the supported allocation, preserves protected bytes and displays correctly in the tested game window.
chapters.note: An offset is not a CPU address. A linear pointer base does not establish a bank-switched mapping. A fixed slot cannot grow just because more words fit in the editor.

details.title: Control codes
details.text: Commands can change colors, insert names, wait for input or end a record. Preserve their declared structure even when they look like punctuation or empty bytes.

details.title: Fonts and graphics
details.text: Glyph painting uses declared graphics storage. Changing a glyph can affect every string that uses it. A layout measurement covers its supplied font and dimensions, not every screen in the game.

chapters.title: Preview sound and respect driver limits
chapters.intro: Native recording captures the game’s mixed output. A decoded sample or note view is an editing preview. Known sequence drivers have separate, bounded readers; a console name does not identify one.
steps: Open Music & sound. Check the identified driver. Mossy Hollow and Hillside have original sequence formats. Other drivers need an implemented reader.
For actual game output, load the source in Playtest, reach the sound, then use Record native preview. Play, pause, seek or loop the resulting preview and save a WAV when useful.

For a supported sample, use a verified offset, allocation, codec and preview sample rate. Choose Check declared sample, then preview gain, reverse, silence or supported WAV replacement before staging. Staged edits update Original and Edited PCM waveform previews; use their play controls when ready. Audio does not autoplay.
Review sound changes, create a sound build and test the real scene. Use note/event or transpose operations only when a supported sequence definition is identified.
chapters.result: The decoded preview corresponds to the intended declared sample, and the game plays the built result at the expected rate and without an unintended neighboring change.
chapters.note: A valid sample codec does not locate a sample or establish its instrument, loop or rate. Re-encoding may be lossy. Note sketches omit game instruments and effects. Verify the built result in native playback.

details.title: Two preview paths
details.text: Native recording captures the engine's mixed output for the selected game session. A declared sample preview decodes a bounded stored resource. They answer different questions and can sound different.

chapters.title: Extract and reinsert supported compression
chapters.intro: A decoded resource must return through a checked parent allocation or a separately reviewed reserved move. Preview recompression shows the exact capacity before planning.
steps: In Resources, open Compressed resources. Choose LZ10, RLE or SNES LC_LZ2 only when the stream format is documented. Confirm its file offset and reserved allocation; a plausible decode does not establish ownership.
Extract the decoded resource into the project. Inspect and edit it through the normal supported editors, then create the edited decoded build.
Select that edited decoded build and review recompression into its original parent. Read the proposed compressed length and confirmed capacity.
Create the parent build only when the stream fits. Inspect the independently decoded comparison, then playtest the actual game resource.
chapters.result: The encoded stream fits without overwriting neighbors, and independent decoding reconstructs every intended decoded byte.
chapters.note: LC_LZ2 has no unique magic signature, so it requires an explicit declared location; the initial signature scan does not guess these streams. LC_LZ3 and other variants are separate formats and are not accepted as LC_LZ2. Recompression is checked by a separately implemented decoder; native playtesting checks how the game consumes the edited data.

details.title: Parent and child
details.text: Extraction creates a resource with an explicit relationship to its parent bytes. Editing a child does not automatically modify the game. Reinsert the selected child build and test the resulting parent ROM.

details.title: Capacity and relocation limits
details.text: Recompression stays inside its declared parent allocation. The separate Advanced data-move workflow checks explicitly declared linear references and reserved space; it does not discover compressed-stream ownership or make an oversized reinsertion safe. Follow the data-relocation chapter rather than increasing capacity to silence a failure.

details.title: Format reference
details.text: The LC_LZ2 format follows the documented five-command encoding, including big-endian absolute repeat offsets: SMW Editor compression reference. The encoder is original deterministic code, not an optimal-size guarantee.

chapters.caption: Actual SNES LC_LZ2 inspection before extraction. The original demonstration uses a direct-literal palette chunk; the original codec also tests fill, increment and repeating-reference commands.

chapters.title: Record routes and compare builds
chapters.intro: A regression route repeats explicit inputs and checks an expected observation. Define what should remain unchanged and what is intentionally different.
steps: Open Routes and start recording controller inputs. Reach the screen in Playtest, pause and capture a measured frame for the selected build.
In Screenshot checkpoints, select a stable region up to 256 x 256 pixels. Add the checkpoint to the latest recorded input, then stop and save the recording.
Replay the recorded checkpoint. For original/build comparison, save a cold-start definition, open Regression, select the original, build and up to eight routes, then run the suite.
Read baseline, build and assertion results separately. Inspect expected, actual and difference images on a failure. Rerun after fixing a relevant change.
chapters.result: The baseline passes its defined assertions before the build is evaluated. Results are bound to the measured source, engine and route setup.
chapters.note: A passing region or route covers that observation. It does not certify the entire game. Timing, random state, blinking or scrolling can make an unsuitable screenshot reference unstable.

details.title: Choose assertions deliberately
details.text: For a palette edit, capture the changed interface and an unchanged scene. For a balance edit, compare the stored value and a repeatable in-game action. A detected intentional difference can be expected.

details.title: Smoke checks
details.text: Check ROM runs a short 120-frame fresh-worker test and measures output. It can establish startup evidence, but it is not a campaign test, a save-system test or a substitute for explicit expected gameplay.

details.title: Progression coverage
details.text: Routes also expose Progression coverage. Select authenticated route records and declare required, optional, ending and unknown objectives, then build the coverage graph. Unvisited objectives stay separate; imported PASS labels do not grant coverage. An advanced declared resource model states supplied action costs and assumptions rather than inferring combat rules.

chapters.title: Inspect memory and translate addresses
chapters.intro: File offsets, console addresses and emulator memory regions describe different spaces. Declare the mapping before comparing or editing them.
steps: Start with exact source/build bytes and a known offset. Use the number inspector to choose signedness and byte order rather than guessing from a displayed decimal value.

In Address explorer, choose the supported Declared mapping and required bank/bounds, then Resolve address. Use Inspect mapped bytes to open that current source location. An active hardware bank is not observed by this declaration.

Load a matching Playtest session. Under Find a changing value, use Start RAM search, play one action, pause, then Capture & narrow by changed, unchanged, increased, decreased or exact value. Add a watch to a measured result.

Use the native capture workflow for actual access events. Declared mappings, imported traces and changed RAM values remain separate evidence types. The recorded context is a lead, not proof of game meaning or DMA ownership.
chapters.result: The translated location uses the intended mapping and bank. A watch reports the selected memory value for the actual loaded session.
chapters.note: A changed value does not identify the instruction that wrote it. A byte pattern match is not proof that the same code or structure exists in a different revision.

details.title: Tables and pointers
details.text: For a declared linear table pointer, target file offset = stored value - base. Record stride is the distance between entries; a field offset is relative to each record. Bank switching needs additional mapping evidence. Find declared references follows only supplied mappings; undeclared code uses remain unknown.

details.title: Memory is not a ROM location
details.text: RAM matches do not identify the stored ROM source of a value. Available video-memory previews decode exposed bytes as indexed grayscale tiles; palette, object attributes and ROM ownership remain unknown. Use repeated controlled observations to narrow a candidate.

chapters.title: Reuse checked recipes and definitions
chapters.intro: A recipe repeats supported source-bound operations. A definition describes storage. Neither import grants arbitrary shell execution or native evidence trust.
steps: Open Advanced > Recipes & definitions and select the exact original source revision.
After reviewing or building edits, use Save a plan as a recipe, or import an existing recipe JSON file. Keep the recipe with its source identity and intended purpose.
Preview every operation and affected range on rerun. Resolve wrong hashes, overlaps and unsupported commands before creating a new build.

Export checked Text, Graphics & fonts, Stats & data, Levels & objects or Music & sound definitions in Resource definitions. Reimport the JSON on the same source, choose Check and import definition and inspect the decoded result before editing.
chapters.result: The recipe produces a fresh reviewable plan for the exact source and rejects stale or incompatible assumptions. The new build remains separate.
chapters.note: A recipe from a trusted person can still target a different revision. Inspect the plan rather than treating the filename or previous success as authority.

details.title: Batch table changes
details.text: The table editor previews up to 1,024 source records. Choose set, add, multiply or percent, then inspect the range. Percent changes round halves away from zero; numeric overflow is refused. Game-specific limits still require evidence.

details.title: Checked definition exchange
details.text: The exported envelope records source SHA-256 and size, resource kind and checked definition. Level object metadata and sound layouts travel as declarations, not runtime proof. Wrong sources or invalid definitions refuse; ROM files and native reports are excluded. Existing version-1 definitions keep their format.

chapters.title: Use AI and MCP with explicit permissions
chapters.intro: ROMancer works without AI. Compatible clients can use its local MCP stdio adapter to inspect supported data and, when explicitly enabled, create checked builds.
steps: Open Settings > AI & LLM access to create a client configuration with the correct interpreter and workspace. The root README documents the command-line entry point.
Start with read-only access. The source entry point is python -B -m romancer.mcp_server --workspace <workspace-folder>. Use the installed interpreter for the bundled edition.
Enable writes with --allow-writes only for a deliberate editing session. Add --rom-root <folder> for each dedicated folder from which that client may import ROMs.
Require the same inspect, plan, build, playtest and patch-verification cycle. Review generated plans and sharing content yourself. Keep ROMs, save data and personal paths private.
chapters.result: The client uses structured supported operations against the intended workspace. Read-only mode refuses writes, and imported sources stay within explicitly allowed roots.
chapters.note: MCP is an optional transport, not a built-in model or proof of game semantics. Source identity, numeric budgets, current runtime context and read/write permissions still apply to each structured call.

details.title: Bounded investigation operations
details.text: The exposed tools include explicit address resolution, declared references, bounded byte explanations, memory searches and watches, exposed video-tile inspection and supported compression checks. Use the client's available-tool list and input schemas first. system.operations describes backend operations; some are not exposed through MCP. Some observations create temporary search state or saved ranges and therefore require write-enabled access; they do not write arbitrary native RAM.

details.title: Definitions and permissions
details.text: Definition exchange is source-bound and requires writes when it creates or stores an export. Native investigation also has typed, bounded capture operations; its separate replay starts from power on. No arbitrary shell, caller-supplied debugger script or continuous live breakpoint control is exposed. Discover current schemas before sending arguments.

details.title: The same current tools
details.text: Read editing.readiness before choosing an editor. sound.system returns known music definitions. With explicit writes, sound.plan followed by build.apply uses the same service as the GUI. Query system.operations and the MCP tool list for the available operations.

details.title: New investigation and editing operations
details.text: debugger.follow summarizes authenticated full captures; definitions.preview/save uses source/research-bound review digests; references.survey reports exact numeric candidates; commands.inspect/plan protects opcode bytes; animations.list/get/preview/save/delete manages declared arrangements. Read-only mode exposes inspections, not saving or plan operations. Writes retain explicit --allow-writes and allowed import roots.

details.title: Read-only coverage status
details.text: coverage.status lists the frozen 942 exact target identities with bounded query, system_filter, page and limit arguments. Current accepted revisions: zero. A catalog match is not a decoded game. Evidence metadata preflight cannot certify a revision or authorize ROM writes.

details.title: Generic editing acceptance
details.text: The same source-bound inspect, draft history, plan, build and independently verified patch export path passed all 942 frozen inputs. This verifies file operations for the supplied revisions. A game-specific edit still needs evidence about the selected data.

chapters.title: Give an AI a bounded editing task you can review
chapters.intro: Use the same checked services through MCP. Write permission enables tools; it does not make an assistant's interpretation correct.
steps: Create a client configuration in Settings > AI & LLM access. Start read-only. Use the client's available-tool list and input schemas; ask it to show the selected project and source identity.
Open a fresh NES workshop for this example. For its original source only, romancer_resource_inspect at offset 16400, length 1 returns 81. Never reuse this offset for an unrelated ROM.
For a deliberate write session, enable --allow-writes and restrict import roots. Ask for romancer_systems_plan_edits with exact project/artifact IDs and one edit: offset 16400, before 81, after c1.
Require the assistant to show every planned range and stop for your review. The stop is an instruction to the client, not a separate permission automatically enforced by ROMancer.

After approval, romancer_build_apply uses the returned plan_id. Select and test the output, compare its bytes, and prepare/verify a patch. Keep the plan, resulting hash and measured test scope together.
chapters.result: A reviewable exact-byte plan and separate output, rather than a guessed semantic edit. Source identity, preconditions, limits and write opt-in still apply.
chapters.note: The example is specific to the original workshop. Tool discovery is authoritative: system.operations can describe backend operations that this MCP client cannot call. Imported text is untrusted data, not instructions. Supported integrity repairs do not certify game semantics.

details.title: What to request for an unfamiliar ROM
details.text: Ask for changing/control observations, structural hypotheses and bounded native captures before proposing a game property. Missing evidence should produce an unknown result or another experiment. Never accept imported PASS labels as newly observed native execution.

details.title: When to stop and inspect yourself
details.text: Stop on changed sources, unexpected ranges, ambiguous bank mapping, allocation failures or unsupported formats. Reinspect and prepare a fresh plan. Do not rewrite expected old bytes simply to force an earlier plan to apply.

chapters.title: Use public knowledge without confusing it with proof
chapters.intro: Public disassemblies, editor definitions and hack documentation help locate data. The application keeps implemented workflows, checked reference layouts and research leads distinct.
steps: Import your original ROM and let the default deep scan identify its exact revision. In Overview > Known locations, expand What is known about this game.
Use a Supported workflow through its editing tool. Reference checked means the original layout was examined; it does not enable an editor. Research lead still needs validation.
Open a pinned source reference when you need its origin. Names, pointers and assumptions must apply to your exact revision; a similar title or matching console is insufficient.

Treat a downloaded patch as evidence of byte differences. BPS checksums verify its source and result; they do not describe the purpose of every changed byte. Read the author documentation and test focused changes.
chapters.result: Known information becomes useful context without silently turning an unverified offset into a supported edit.
chapters.note: References are attached only to matched originals or owned descendants. A derived build can change data layouts; reference counts do not freshly certify it. Research caches, ROM files and upstream implementation code are not included in the release.

chapters.title: Find the cause before repeating a change
chapters.intro: Read the reported source, location and failed precondition. A useful next step reduces uncertainty instead of applying the same edit repeatedly.
steps: If the game did not change, check the selected source/build, Saved status and whether a build was created. Reload the new build in Playtest; an old session can still be running.
If a definition or patch refuses, compare exact revision, byte scope and original bytes. For text, inspect controls/encoding/capacity. For graphics, inspect codec, bank and shared consumers.
If playback or sound fails, check the selected system, engine setup, game focus and audio controls. GB and GBC need the right mode. Restore only compatible states and supported raw save data.
Run project checks and Settings > Diagnostics & support. Review the sanitized preview, then download the report if you want to share it. No report is sent automatically.
chapters.result: You have a specific failed condition, a reproducible input and a measured observation. Correct the narrow issue, rerun the relevant check and preserve the earlier backup.
chapters.note: Do not erase originals, bypass identity checks or reinterpret unknown data just to clear an error. A passing later check should address the actual earlier failure.

details.title: Useful support detail
details.text: State the operation, application revision, selected system, expected result and actual result. Review any screenshot or log for personal information before sharing. Sanitized reports exclude ROM/save bytes, credentials, personal paths, project names and raw errors. The three checklists that follow cover identity and patch problems, editing problems, and playback or recovery problems. Each gives a meaning and a next step.

details.title: Recovery order
details.text: Keep unsaved text, back up the project, check the source identity, reproduce one small step, inspect the failure and restore or correct the narrow change. Historical reports are references; run fresh native checks for a current claim. For a room destination or mapped-address issue, inspect its checked definition and exact source bytes before treating the result as runtime behavior.

chapters.title: ROM and patch problems
chapters.intro: Start here when an import, identity check or downloaded patch does not match what you expected.
steps: Confirm which file is selected. A source, a modified build and a header-stripped file can have different hashes even when their names look alike.
Read the expected and measured values, comparison scope and patch instructions. Check the region and revision before trying another source.
If the source is correct and a structural check still fails, preserve it and collect the exact failed check. Obtain another verified dump or a documented explanation before editing.
chapters.result: Repeat the relevant check after the correction. Keep the original, the earlier build and your backup available until the new result is confirmed.
chapters.note: A warning explains a limited check. It is not permission to bypass a failed precondition. If the cause remains unknown, keep that resource unchanged and include the operation and measured result in a reviewed support report.

details.title: CRC32 mismatch
details.text: The measured bytes differ from the entered reference. Confirm whole-file versus payload scope, copier prefix, trainer, region and revision. A blank expected value means no reference comparison was performed, not that the dump matched.

details.title: Unknown game or missing named tools
details.text: A valid system header does not identify a game revision. Import a trusted local hash catalog. Use generic inspection or a separately checked definition; a similar filename or another game's offsets are insufficient.

details.title: BPS source mismatch / IPS has no source checksum
details.text: BPS validates its embedded source identity. Choose the exact source required by the patch. IPS does not supply this proof: check an external source reference and the resulting output rather than treating a successful apply as compatibility.

details.title: Header, size or startup warning
details.text: Read which structure failed. Unusual homebrew headers can produce warnings. Unknown mapper state or an unsupported branch form can be Not checked. Investigate those limits; do not call them successful execution.

details.title: Scan limited or interrupted
details.text: A byte, time or result budget limits that analysis. Review completed findings and the named unavailable part. Retry the bounded operation or inspect a smaller declared range. Increasing a budget does not establish missing game semantics.

chapters.title: Editing and preview problems
chapters.intro: Use these checks when a proposed edit is blocked, a preview looks wrong or the game still shows an older value.
steps: Keep the current text or proposal before reloading. Check the selected source/build and the exact resource definition.
Correct the narrow issue, then request a fresh review. An old plan cannot authorize changed source bytes or a different proposal.
Create a separate build and reload that build in Playtest. Compare the intended scene and one nearby unchanged behavior.
chapters.result: Repeat the relevant check after the correction. Keep the original, the earlier build and your backup available until the new result is confirmed.
chapters.note: A warning explains a limited check. It is not permission to bypass a failed precondition. If the cause remains unknown, keep that resource unchanged and include the operation and measured result in a reviewed support report.

details.title: The edit is saved, but the game did not change
details.text: Saved refers to the draft. Review changes, create a build, select it in the top bar and reload it in Playtest. A preview notification does not mean that playable ROM bytes were written.

details.title: Text too long, unmapped character or damaged spreadsheet
details.text: Use encoded bytes, not character count. Preserve control codes, stable IDs and original columns; edit only translations. Re-export a fresh sheet and try one short row. Shorten text or establish a supported allocation instead of dropping controls.

details.title: Wrong colors, scrambled tiles or shared edits
details.text: Check codec, source bank, stored palette and tile arrangement. Editor preview colors may be metadata rather than palette bytes. Inspect declared shared consumers before approving a change that appears in several frames or rooms.

details.title: Stale definition, changed source or overlapping edits
details.text: Reinspect the exact source and declared ranges. Reuse a parent definition only through its guarded workflow. Reconcile overlaps and dependencies; obtain a fresh plan rather than forcing expected bytes to match.

details.title: Map, animation, audio or compressed resource unavailable
details.text: A system label does not decode a game-specific format. Use only supported definitions. A sample codec does not find instruments, a frame layout does not decode an animation script, and a map preview does not prove collision. Respect compressed allocation limits.

chapters.title: Playback, saving and recovery problems
chapters.intro: Protect progress first. Check the selected output and session before replacing data or restarting.
steps: Preserve unsaved text and download a backup of exposed battery-save RAM before experimenting with imports or restarts.
Confirm the selected ROM, engine, input device, audio controls and save format. Reproduce one small problem at a time.
Use Projects > Trash to restore an accidentally deleted project. Run fresh checks after restore, then review a sanitized support report if the issue persists.
chapters.result: Repeat the relevant check after the correction. Keep the original, the earlier build and your backup available until the new result is confirmed.
chapters.note: A warning explains a limited check. It is not permission to bypass a failed precondition. If the cause remains unknown, keep that resource unchanged and include the operation and measured result in a reviewed support report.

details.title: Application will not finish opening
details.text: Keep the complete portable folder together. Use the supplied launcher or installed shortcut; inspect startup details. Check file access and the local service. Retry after correcting the reported problem. Preserve the workspace when reinstalling.

details.title: No game input or sound
details.text: Load the intended build in Playtest. Select the connected controller/type and give the game focus. Check mute, volume and output controls. An unknown sequence driver does not prevent supported native audio recording.

details.title: Save state refused / battery save has the wrong size
details.text: States require the same ROM bytes, engine and setup. Use the state with its matching output. Battery files are separate raw persistent RAM; use the expected exact size or export raw data from the originating emulator. Do not pad or truncate an unknown format.

details.title: Test failed or is inconclusive
details.text: Open Original, Build and Difference pictures where recorded. Check route, start state, frame, comparison region and assertion. An incomplete run is not a pass; a visual difference can be intended. Rerun after correcting the specific test setup or edit.

details.title: Draft save, backup or restore failed
details.text: Keep the window open and copy unsaved text. Check write access, available space and the active workspace. Do not remove an active writer's lock. Restore from a complete private backup or Trash, then recheck files and run fresh tests.

details.title: Read the actual failure
details.text: An illegal-instruction exit, a missing Windows dependency, a native crash and an observer-script error have distinct messages. A generic failed exit is not automatically a CPU problem. Follow the shown remedy, retry a short capture and export diagnostics if it repeats.

chapters.title: Use documented codes to find investigation leads
chapters.intro: A documented code can narrow a search. Its published effect label is a claim to test, and its CPU address still needs a valid mapping to the selected ROM.
steps: In Resources, expand ROM health & revision, then Code reference catalog. Choose a local UTF-8 TXT, JSON, JSONL, CSV or TSV catalog and click Import code references. This replaces the project’s reference catalog; it does not edit the ROM.
Choose Inspect matching references. Search an effect label or code and use Previous/Next for additional pages. Required + combinations and / revision alternatives remain distinct.

Read the revision status. MATCHED compares supplied hashes with the root source; MISMATCH has no mapped locations. UNSPECIFIED usually means title-only selection. Even a hash match does not verify the effect label.

Use Inspect beside a decoded location to open its bytes. Compare bytes can eliminate incompatible candidates, but a switchable-bank candidate does not establish the active bank. Do not turn an incomplete or truncated combination into a patch.
chapters.result: You can follow a source-attributed clue to actual bounded ROM bytes without silently activating a cheat or trusting another game’s offsets.
chapters.note: Game Genie decoding covers NES, SNES, Genesis, GB and GBC only. Hardware overlays, unknown mappers and unsupported codes remain unresolved. Keep the original local catalog for full provenance when a result is shortened.
chapters.caption: Actual Castlevania reference inspection: one code has no compatible compare byte, while another links to a matching stored byte. Effect labels remain unverified.

details.title: Mixed extracts and duplicate references
details.text: A composite text file may include both publication and community sections. Explicit Game Genie and Action Replay labels stay separate. Unsupported Action Replay records remain reference data without decoded ROM locations. Duplicate publication/community entries retain their own provenance; the record count is not a count of unique, tested effects.

chapters.title: Understand an address before investigating it
chapters.intro: A CPU address, file offset and video-memory offset can have the same number and refer to different things. Hardware help explains the region without pretending to know a game variable.
steps: Open Advanced > Investigation and expand Hardware & address help. A completed ROM scan supplies the CPU, byte-order convention, graphics layout and mapping notes for the selected system.
Choose the address domain, enter a decimal or 0x hexadecimal value, and click Explain address. NES PPU, physical VRAM and SNES audio CPU domains are separate choices only where supported.

Read the region and its conditions. A GB cartridge window may contain RTC registers; a SNES audio port is not audio RAM; Genesis sound RAM requires bus arbitration. Register descriptions never read or write the hardware.

For a persistent ROM edit, use Address explorer with a checked mapping, including the physical bank and header offset. A core’s exposed-memory offset also needs an established mapping before treating it as a CPU address.
chapters.result: You can tell a plausible ROM location from RAM, graphics storage, a device port or an unresolved board-dependent range.
chapters.note: To investigate a changing stat, reproduce one controlled change, narrow its RAM candidates, and establish the writer and immutable source in a debugger that exposes those events. ROMancer’s snapshots do not provide instruction breakpoints or prove causation. Unexecuted bytes and repeated FF/00 runs do not establish free space.

details.title: Standard formats across systems
details.text: Hardware & address help -> Standard graphics formats explains documented tile storage, palette encodings and map attributes for all six choices. These are hardware facts, not a promise that a game stores its ROM resources uncompressed in the same layout.

chapters.title: Read automatic cartridge verification
chapters.intro: Deep scan now displays individual cartridge-health results, including supported startup addresses. These checks describe the stored image without executing its program.
steps: Let the automatic scan finish. Expand Cartridge verification in ROM investigation. Read Consistent, Needs attention, Mismatch and Not checked separately. A warning is not a proof of corruption.

Inspect supported reset vectors or entry branches. CPU addresses and file locations remain different. Click a vector/header or target-byte button to examine its actual storage. An unresolved bank state does not receive a guessed target.
For GB/GBC, read the documented header checks. Logo comparison uses fingerprints rather than distributed logo assets; custom headers can intentionally differ.

For ordinary LoROM/HiROM up to 4 MiB, checksum verification handles standard tail mirroring and an identified copier header. The size declaration uses the rounded-up payload size. Enhancement chips, extended maps and unresolved layouts remain outside this checksum rule.
chapters.result: A valid non-power-of-two standard SNES image can be checked correctly, and all six systems get startup checks within their supported mappings and encodings.
chapters.note: NES has no standard whole-cartridge checksum. A standard header logo and an in-bounds branch do not prove game identity, valid target instructions, authentic firmware, or successful gameplay. Use native capture for bounded actual access events. It is separate from these static cartridge checks and does not provide continuous live break/continue control.

chapters.title: Trace native accesses and inspect their source context
chapters.intro: A changed RAM value is a lead. A native capture adds real access callbacks, execution context and supported source mappings.
steps: Open Advanced > Investigation > Trace actual accesses, or investigate a captured value. A value investigation derives a supported physical watch from authenticated core memory. Manual watches use an explicit CPU address and read/write/execution kind; Genesis supports read/write watches and separately ordered instruction samples.

The full Windows package includes MesenCE and is ready to capture every system except Genesis. The first Genesis capture downloads the official MAME 0.289 release once (about 84 MiB) after you confirm it. In a source-only build, choose Prepare debugger if needed. Pinned tools are downloaded and checked once; no ROM is uploaded. Native captures are Windows-only.
Choose Replay last Playtest change when an observation includes compatible cold-start inputs, or set up a custom replay. The debugger starts from power on in a separate session.

Choose Capture route for a bounded sample, or Stop at a watched access and set Watched access number. The focused mode uses one explicit watch and stops after that occurrence inside the requested recording window.
Inspect access address, value, execution context and registers. A source button opens its recorded file location; Resources explains the association and links back.

Choose Explain this capture. Use a mapped writer to find a ROM address to watch. Under Watch a ROM read during this replay, enter that address and capture reads. Inspect ROM bytes opens a mapped read with its recorded context.

A focused result says Stopped at requested access only after the native protocol confirms the occurrence. Inspect that event’s registers and execution context. No matching occurrence, truncation and a budget stop are different outcomes.
chapters.result: A durable native capture with mapped writer context, separate source-read locations, resource overlaps and a concrete next experiment. Historical and partial status remain visible.
chapters.note: Focused stops do not take a graphics snapshot or resume a libretro save state. Original and real supplied ROMs were checked across all six systems. An observed access/context is evidence; higher-level semantics and causal ownership still need investigation.

chapters.title: Edit and arrange known event commands
chapters.intro: Events & commands decodes a supplied command grammar into named instructions and fixed integer parameters. It does not discover a scripting language or execute a script.
steps: Open Advanced > Investigation > Events & commands. Expand Build a documented command format to enter opcode, command name, total byte count and role. Add named operands with byte position, width, byte order and integer bounds, then add the command to the grammar.

Add the documented script ID, name, file offset and reserved byte count. Preview known format runs the real decoder. Save only after reviewing it; replacing an existing setup requires acknowledgement. Advanced JSON supports larger grammars and pointer fields.

Each operand declares offset within the command, bytes 1–4, little/big endian, minimum, maximum and optional target_base. Byte 0 is the opcode and cannot be edited. For a declared pointer operand, target file offset = stored value − target_base.

Choose Inspect commands. Unknown instructions, truncated operands, invalid values or a missing declared end leave that script read-only. At most 32 scripts, 256 command types, 256 decoded commands per script and 2,048 commands overall are handled.

For sequence changes, expand Arrange a linear command sequence. Insert before the selected row, remove or move commands, then stage their named values. Supply the confirmed unused-tail byte and acknowledge that no outside consumer enters the script’s middle. Preview, review and create the build.

Preview and save a definition only after reviewing its structure. Game view connects the saved script and its commands. Declared target references can connect to existing resources, and author links can record triggers, destinations, collision or animation relationships.
chapters.result: Fixed parameter changes preserve opcodes. Sequence edits can change the order and count of fully declared linear commands inside the original allocation. Reopened builds are freshly inspected; the exact same recorded plan can reopen its existing build.
chapters.note: Sequence editing requires exactly one final end command and all stored command bytes declared. Branches, pointer-bearing commands, unknown bytes, bad tail fill and overflow refuse. End is an editor role, not proof of a native instruction. Native event behavior still needs testing.

chapters.title: Test repeated layouts and open a neutral table editor
chapters.intro: Repeated numeric layouts can help locate tables or possible pointer arrays. ROMancer tests the bytes without assigning invented game labels.
steps: Open Investigation > Explore ROM structure. Test a window up to 65536 bytes. Deep-scan summaries state their smaller sampled coverage.
Compare candidate starts, counts, strides, widths and byte orders. Target previews use only bytes inside the inspected window.
Keep Neutral numeric values for ordinary editing. A linear-pointer interpretation is an explicit hypothesis: file offset = stored value - base.
Choose Open table editor. ROMancer reproduces the candidate from current bytes and validates its layout. Finish existing staged table edits first. Choose Save this layout to retain it.
Edit a value, review the before/after plan and create a separate build. Playtest. Gather access evidence before assigning names such as health or damage.
chapters.result: A checked neutral editor connected to the normal review, build and verified patch workflow.
chapters.note: Tests cover 16/24/32-bit runs, both byte orders, bounded strides and explicit file-relative pointer hypotheses. Several layouts can fit. A generated editor does not prove all consumers, relocation safety or game meaning.

chapters.title: Set up or repair native investigation
chapters.intro: The full Windows edition includes the reviewed MesenCE observer, separate from the everyday playtesting engines. MAME for Genesis is downloaded once on first use. Source-only builds can prepare a pinned cache. Native captures are Windows-only.
steps: Open Investigation > Trace actual accesses. Check observer availability. The full Windows edition already includes MesenCE. Windows x64 is required; Genesis uses MAME and also needs an x86-64-v2 CPU.

For the first Genesis capture, or in a source-only build, choose Prepare debugger. After you confirm, the official MAME 0.289 release is downloaded once (about 84 MiB). Fixed official HTTPS artifacts are checked by exact size and SHA-256. No caller-supplied executable or download URL is accepted.

Bundled observers and prepared caches work offline after verification. The full Windows package retains complete matching observer source and licenses. Prepared upstream tools keep their own source records and notices.

If bundled checks fail, reinstall the current full package; an old cache cannot replace it silently. In source-only mode, Prepare debugger preserves a changed cache while activating a verified replacement. No ROM is uploaded.
chapters.result: A checked bundled observer or prepared cache, available to both the interface and typed MCP operations.
chapters.note: Bundled MesenCE retains its upstream license and complete corresponding source. The downloaded MAME is the unmodified official release under its own license. The original ROMancer wrapper remains MIT licensed. Exact hashes establish the distributed files, not an independent audit of every upstream build input.

details.title: If an observer exits unexpectedly

chapters.title: Move or grow declared data without losing its references
chapters.kicker: Declared data / exact references / separate build
chapters.intro: Move data only after investigating its consumers and reserving the destination. Matching fill bytes cannot prove unused space.
steps: Open Resources > Move declared data. Enter source allocation, reserved destination, sizes, fill and alignment. Banked cartridges require an explicit same-bank constraint.
Optionally import edited data up to 48 KiB. It must fit the destination. Cartridge size and the original extent are preserved.
Declare every external linear pointer: file offset, width, byte order, encoding adjustment and interior offset. Existing stored values are checked. Code and embedded pointers are unsupported.
Confirm reference completeness and destination reservation. Review pointer before/after values, then create a separate build. These confirmations are author declarations.
Choose Inspect moved data. Old fixed-offset declarations are not reused. A wholly covered neutral table can be rebased; inspect it and Save this layout.

chapters.title: Share checked definitions and research
chapters.intro: A research pack carries the active supported resource definitions and notes in one JSON file. It is meant for repeating work on the same exact ROM revision. Saved whole-object layouts can travel in a research-v2 pack for the same exact source.
steps: In Resources, expand Share or import research. Choose Export research pack, then Download research JSON. Review the file before sharing; notes, references and definition byte guards can contain material you entered.
In the destination project select the matching ROM. Choose the JSON file and Review selected pack. A different ROM hash, size, system or invalid definition is refused.
Read the definition and note counts and the replacement list. Explicitly acknowledge replacements before choosing Import reviewed research. Other notes remain.
Import validates the whole pack again and commits metadata together. If the source, document or current research changed since review, review again. It never writes ROM bytes.
Use the Resource browser to open an imported layout. A different existing setup draft gets its own review and recovery copy; it is not silently discarded.

Research-v3 packs also carry saved animation layouts and their exact graphics schemas. Imported arrangements stay author declarations and never become native proof. Command definitions use the same source-bound preview and replacement review as other declarations.
chapters.result: The imported definitions inspect the destination source and the original notes remain searchable. Compare the source hash before and after; it must be identical.
chapters.note: Packs are limited to 1 MiB and are not executable extensions. They contain neither emulator states nor game saves. They do not make a new game revision compatible. AI clients use research.inspect, research.note_get, research.preview and research.apply with the same guards. Object layouts retain flips and shared uses, but imported layouts deliberately lose local proof references and fresh runtime authority. Inspect names, source references and screenshots before sharing. A research pack may contain byte guards or decoded research from your ROM; it is not automatically safe to publish merely because it is JSON.

chapters.title: Use published Pokemon and Mario research
chapters.intro: Help and Resources include a searchable library of pinned public research for Pokemon Red/Blue, Crystal, Super Mario Bros. and Super Mario World.
steps: Expand Popular-game references and search for Pokemon or Mario. Read the documented facts and use Primary source for the pinned project version. Links require a network connection; the bundled summaries work offline.

Keep address domains separate. For example, the published Super Mario Bros. lives counter is CPU RAM 0x075A, not a ROM file offset. Player power-up form at 0x0756 is a different concept from the movement-state variable.
Choose the correct documented prefix and Preview table layout. Red/Blue uses five base stats after its Dex number; Crystal separates special attack/defense.

Inspect values and record identities in the proposed Data table. Save this layout only when the declaration is correct. Use the normal reviewed table build to make changes; omitted fields and padding stay outside the prefix.
chapters.result: You have a useful source-linked lead or a checked table proposal, with no false claim that an arbitrary Pokemon or Mario hack uses the original layout.
chapters.note: Published structure facts do not locate a table automatically or prove compatibility with a modified game. Establish the correct table base, stride and record count, preview the actual values, then save the checked layout.

chapters.title: Find named ROM addresses with symbol files
chapters.intro: A matching symbol listing connects human-readable names to addresses. ROMancer reads RGBDS bank:address listings for Game Boy and Game Boy Color.
steps: Obtain the symbol file produced for your exact game build. In Resources, expand Named addresses from a symbol file. Choose the listing and its supported format, then Review symbol file.
Read entry and ignored-line counts. This text format has no embedded ROM identity, so confirm that it belongs to the selected build before importing the reviewed names.
Search a symbol name. Inspect bytes opens a mapped location inside the selected ROM. RAM and I/O symbols show the CPU address and do not offer a ROM byte button.
Keep code entry semantics separate: odd GNU code addresses are not automatically converted into Thumb code offsets. A missing or ambiguous mapping must be resolved before editing.
The import stores source-bound metadata and an owned copy of the listing. It does not modify ROM bytes, add instructions, infer field sizes or authorize an edit.
chapters.result: Navigate a declared ROM label without confusing it with a RAM value. A symbol listing has no embedded ROM hash: acknowledge its relationship to this exact build before importing.
chapters.note: UTF-8 listings are limited to 2 MiB and 65,536 entries; results page in groups of 50. Duplicate names at different addresses remain separate. GNU nm listings are supported; arbitrary linker map grammars are not.

chapters.title: Declare relationships and use evidence safely
chapters.kicker: Connected storage / measured pixels / authored meaning
chapters.intro: Connected editing keeps three things distinct: checked storage declarations, native observations and user interpretations. Saving a relationship adds project metadata without changing ROM bytes.
steps: Select a resource in Game view and expand Add a declared relationship. Choose another currently listed resource, a relationship and an evidence note, then Save declared link.
Use Remove link to remove that authored relationship. A declared link is not promoted to a proven runtime reference, and a range overlap does not establish ownership.

Native traces are authenticated by this local application. A restored or imported trace remains useful history, but cannot authorize opening a fresh candidate for editing. Capture new evidence for the current source.
If an indexed trace is missing or damaged, capture again. Valid existing trace references are preserved; unavailable references are repaired without deleting evidence files.

Use the existing CPU access investigation separately when a supported debugger can observe transfers. The shared pixel-trace service does not fabricate instruction traces for systems without that capture capability.
chapters.result: The same graph can connect resources from any supported console while preserving the difference between observation and interpretation.
chapters.note: Resource lists page by 50. Detail views show up to 32 connections. Generic unnamed numeric tables sample their first 256 rows; named catalogs retain their declared records. Graph and trace limits remain visible rather than silently implying complete coverage.

chapters.title: Use connected editing from automation and MCP
chapters.kicker: Shared services / strict inputs / reproducible checks
chapters.intro: The GUI and MCP call the same source-bound graph, trace, declaration and build-check services. No external AI account is required by ROMancer itself.
steps: Use gameview.graph to search and page resources, then gameview.detail for fields, byte previews, neighbors and compact image previews. Save or remove your metadata with gameview.link and gameview.unlink.
Load a native worker, capture its current frame, then call traces.capture with that measured frame hash, region and source range. Client-submitted pixels are not accepted as native evidence.

Read traces.get and inspect candidates before calling traces.open with explicitly selected match indices. Follow the resulting checked editor setup through the normal reviewable plan/build operations.

Save checks.configure with automatic, mode, bounded input steps, optional region and completed route IDs. Call checks.run for a source and target; poll the returned job and retrieve checks.status or checks.get.

Retain source, build and core hashes and exact result statuses. Stop on stale sources, unsupported layouts, failed assertions or unavailable workers rather than inventing an offset or a successful check.
chapters.result: Beginners can use the visual workflow, while advanced clients can reproduce its evidence and edits through strict operation schemas.
chapters.note: Checks allow up to 20 input steps and 2400 frames; original twice plus build once. Fresh workers verify next-frame save-state replay and close after the check. Restored evidence is historical. A passing configured test never means every possible game action was tested.

chapters.title: Read a recovered pixel map and its byte lanes
chapters.kicker: Verified graphic sources / evidence and controls
chapters.intro: A source code is assigned to each stored pixel. Separate native runs reveal which screen pixels carry those codes. Two additional spatial patterns test the recovered mapping; palette-only effects cannot satisfy the required distinct pixel origins.
steps: The original must reproduce the exact captured RGB frame twice, using the same effective core options, controller setup and system-file hashes. A different second-run context is inconclusive even if the pictures look identical.

Seven coded probes identify an 8 by 8 source; an 8 by 16 source can need eight. At least 16 distinct source pixel IDs, spread across rows and columns, must be recovered. A global recolor has too few distinct origins to qualify.

Two independent color-balanced validation patterns must reproduce every accepted mapped pixel. Each tested color needs changed and unchanged spatial witnesses. Failed validation does not cherry-pick a smaller passing subset.

Expand Recovered pixel origins. Source pixel coordinates lead to encoded file-byte lanes and bit masks, then to screen coordinates. Byte lanes are derived from the tested codec; they are not a native bus-read log.

The final control reverses the probe plan, restores the exact original ROM hash and reproduces its whole frame. Worker exits, plan hashes and execution identities are recorded. Diagnostic copies are removed after teardown.
chapters.result: You can follow a measured screen pixel back to its literal source pixel and the codec-defined bytes that store it. The displayed mask uses screen orientation, including flipped or partial placements.
chapters.note: Compression, transformed graphics, shared storage and unstable startup can remain unresolved. Failed tests never authorize a verified source edit.

chapters.title: Resolve an unverified source and edit safely
chapters.kicker: Verified graphic sources / evidence and controls
chapters.intro: A refusal is useful evidence. It separates a genuine source from a coincidental pattern, a shared effect or an unreproducible scene. Use a focused next experiment rather than changing an unproved address.
steps: No literal match: choose another part or source range. Keep the coverage limits in view. Compressed or RAM-generated graphics need a supported decoder or further native investigation; this tool does not guess their format.
Replay unavailable: reload the game and capture a fresh trace. State restores, battery saves, changed options and histories over 36,000 frames or 2048 steps cannot become cold-start proof.

Too few distinct origins or a color effect: choose a larger, more detailed visible part. A flat or nearly transparent region may not have enough independently testable pixels. A global palette change is not literal tile provenance.

Validation failed or original changed: retain the report, try a stable scene and inspect shared storage. Earlier positive tests remain available. Imported reports cannot authorize a verified editor handoff.

After editing, review the build and playtest the changed scene. Observed colors preview the original; palette bytes are unchanged. Choose a known color index or declare a palette. Source verification does not certify a later modification.

chapters.title: Inspect actual graphics reads, writes and video memory
chapters.intro: Source verification tests a ROM-to-picture dependency. A native graphics capture adds a separate access trail and a measured video-memory snapshot. The two kinds of evidence answer different questions.
steps: Save a fresh cold-start trace in Playtest. Expand Native graphics accesses & video memory. Set a focused ROM span up to 2048 bytes, and choose Record native accesses. The trace must fit 3600 frames and 64 supported input steps without truncation.

The reviewed observer replays the route in an isolated process. NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Color and SMS use MesenCE; Genesis uses MAME. The full Windows package includes MesenCE and its corresponding source; MAME is downloaded once, after you confirm, for the first Genesis capture.

Read the event page: access kind, physical memory domain or CPU-bus address, measured file offset where mapping was established, value and native operation kind. Move between pages. Omitted-event counts show when a capture budget was reached.

Inspect the final scene and registers. Choose the pattern/video-memory domain, offset and tested tile codec to preview 32 complete stored tiles. Grayscale shows indices; it does not guess a palette or a ROM origin.

Reopen saved captures through Game view or their capture ID. Pair the trail with a verified visual source or a controlled value investigation. Export reusable layouts and notes as checked research, keeping runtime evidence local and source-bound.
chapters.result: You can distinguish a measured ROM read, a video-memory write, a backend-reported DMA operation and a literal picture dependency. Genesis bus addresses remain bus observations unless a physical source mapping was established. These snapshots are from the end of a separate native replay, not the live Playtest state. Mid-frame banks, palettes and layer changes may differ. Nearby reads and writes do not prove dataflow, decompression ownership or a DMA channel. A callback parameter width is not necessarily the CPU instruction access width. Budget omissions are not absence-of-access proof.
chapters.note: This is a separate native replay. End-of-capture memory may differ from mid-frame state. Read/write adjacency is not dataflow. A callback width is not an instruction width, and budget omissions are not absence-of-access proof.

chapters.title: Preview compressed size and review a reserved move
chapters.intro: Inspect a supported LZ10 or RLE stream inside its confirmed allocation, edit its decoded resource and preview the exact recompression before planning a parent build.
steps: Extract a known LZ10/RLE stream from its confirmed parent allocation. Edit the decoded child and create a build descended from that child.

Choose the edited decoded build, then Preview recompression. Read packed bytes, confirmed allocation, free bytes or overflow. A separate token parser independently checks the encoded data against the edited decoded bytes.
If the output fits, choose Review reinsertion and Create parent build. Changing the selected child after review invalidates that plan. The source ROM remains unchanged.

If it does not fit, reduce the edit or use Move to reserved space only when you understand its references. Declare the reserved destination, expected fill, capacity, alignment, bank origin/window and the existing linear pointer to the stream start.

The form supports all complete external references. Confirm reservation and completeness only when established. The automation API supports up to 128 explicitly declared references. Review the move and create a separate parent build, then inspect the pointer and playtest the resource in its real scene.

In the reserved-move controls, enter the first reviewed pointer and any additional reviewed pointer offsets, one per line. These UI pointers share the selected width, byte order and encoding adjustment. Mixed encodings remain available through the automation schema.

Optionally expand Look for pointer candidates. Survey at most 1 MiB at a time for exact matches to the selected target/encoding/alignment. Add individual candidates only after checking their use. At most 256 are retained; 32 are shown per focused window. Narrow the window to review more.

Acknowledge the complete reference set and reserved destination, then review the move. A matching fill byte does not prove free space. Build and playtest the relocated result; the previous compressed stream is preserved.
chapters.result: The original SNES LC_LZ2 example was independently decoded, edited through ROMancer, recompressed within its allocation, built and compared in native playback. Moving a stream additionally needs reserved storage and all required pointer consumers; passing one example does not identify another game’s compression.
chapters.note: Fill bytes alone do not prove unused space, and numeric pointer matches do not prove completeness. Interior pointers into compressed streams, embedded references, position-dependent code and cross-bank moves remain unavailable. The API refuses an external replacement that could bypass the verified recompression. A pointer survey tests numeric encodings only. Undeclared consumers, other banks, embedded pointers and references outside its window remain unproven. SMS moves require declared same-bank bounds and protect the boot and recognized header extents.

chapters.title: Automate connected editing with the same safeguards
chapters.intro: AI and script clients use the same source-bound services as the visual editor. Work from measured evidence, keep ranges bounded and review separate builds.
steps: Use objects.create with verification_id/match_id pairs from one authenticated frame. objects.list/get/open/delete manage exact-revision layouts. Imported layouts retain declarations only.

Use graphics.accesses.capture for a saved cold route and focused ROM span. Read get in pages, memory up to 4096 bytes, or tiles up to 64 cells. Native scenes arrive as bounded model-visible image blocks.

Use compression.preview_reinsert before plan_reinsert or plan_relocate. Moves require a reserved allocation and every declared external stream-start reference. Raw replacements cannot bypass recompression checks.
Call checks.from_trace with source_id, target_id and trace_id after creating a reviewed build. Changed execution context and unrelated targets are refused. Read the comparison images and status.

Enable MCP writes explicitly and configure allowed import roots. research.export/preview/apply exchange checked metadata on the same exact source. Preserve receipts and have a person review gameplay changes.
chapters.result: Automation can locate verified source parts, open connected objects, inspect actual native observations, plan safe edits and test a descendant build without a model-specific editing backend.
chapters.note: Matching pixels, nearby accesses, author declarations and imported history retain distinct meanings. The application validates source hashes and evidence for both people and automation.

chapters.title: Edit a verified music sequence
chapters.intro: Mossy Hollow and Hillside have identified original pulse sequences. Other games need their own implemented and checked driver format. Sample viewing and native mixed audio recording remain separate workflows.
steps: Open the original editing studio and choose Music & sound. Select its original melody.
Click a note in the piano roll or select its event index. Stage a note, duration or volume change. Undo restores the previous draft.
Preview the original and edited pulse sketches. They show note changes; they do not replace native playback.
Review the byte plan, name a separate build, playtest the melody and export a verified patch.
chapters.result: The original practice melody has a readable piano roll, before/after note values and an independently testable build.
chapters.note: This is an original practice driver, not a universal commercial music decoder. Undecoded game sequences stay unavailable for note editing.
chapters.caption: Original practice melody and staged note controls in the Music & sound editor.

chapters.title: Make room for a longer decoded message
chapters.intro: Use this when a checked fixed-slot message is too long. The original slot stays intact; the reviewed build moves the encoded message and redirects its declared record-start pointers.
steps: In Text & layout, edit the decoded segments. The ordinary capacity warning still describes the old slot. Expand Make room for longer text and choose the record.
Enter a reserved file offset and new byte capacity. Under Advanced, check fill byte, alignment, bank size and bank origin. Padding alone never proves free space.

Known schema pointers are included automatically. Add only checked extra references with offset width little/big adjustment; stored pointer = file offset + adjustment. Growing text supports record-start references only; interior pointers are refused because text lengths can shift.
Confirm that every consumer is covered and the destination is reserved. Preview the encoded byte count, preserved controls and pointer changes. Review the move plan, then create the build.

The moved definition reopens against the exact build. Playtest the real font, window, control behavior and every relevant consumer before exporting. Your original and any newer draft edits remain available.
chapters.result: A separate build with a rechecked moved text definition. The original NES example actually displays WELCOME FRIEND! after its message and pointer move.
chapters.note: Only checked writable, position-independent text can move. Unknown encoding, controls requiring their old position, known resource overlap, invalid banks, insufficient capacity or incomplete acknowledgement refuse. This is not automatic discovery of every text pointer.

chapters.title: Reuse an understood editor format safely
chapters.intro: A reusable format pack keeps saved editor layouts for later projects. Exact-source matching is the default; a successful match still needs review before layouts are saved.
steps: On a source with checked saved editor layouts, open Resources > Reusable format library. Save a named local pack with Exact ROM revision. A pack contains declarative metadata, not executable plugins or a copy of the ROM.
To share it, export its JSON file. To use one, import a local JSON pack up to 512 KiB. The library holds up to 32 packs. Invalid stored files can be removed without blocking the list.
Deep scan suggests matching packs. Open the library and choose Preview match; ROMancer checks the console, source identity and every actual editor decoder. A mismatch is not silently accepted.

Protected-region matching is Advanced: explicitly declare the hash regions that guard compatibility. Console and size must agree, protected bytes must match and the editors must inspect successfully. Another revision needs a separate compatibility acknowledgement.

Review listed definition replacements, then Apply reviewed layouts. ROM bytes are unchanged. Existing drafts are separate; reopen the appropriate editor to inspect this source. Export research notes and evidence separately when needed.
chapters.result: Source-bound editor setup can be reused without retyping its grammar, ranges and field names. Scan suggestions do not apply it automatically.
chapters.note: Protected hashes express an author’s compatibility rule; they do not prove game behavior, every pointer or unseen relocated data. Recheck modified ROMs. Library/layout changes invalidate cached scan results. No pack receives gameplay authority just because its JSON imports.
